Trudolyubovka (Former Jewish Colony Lekert) Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This cemetery served Trudolyubovka, a former Jewish colony named for Hirsch Lekert — the Bundist shoemaker executed in 1902 after shooting Vilnius's Governor-General, documented elsewhere in this collection — founded here in 1924. According to Lyubov Trafimovna, born in 1928 in the neighboring village of Kalinovka, Jews were buried here before WWII, after which Orthodox Christians took over the site, making it a mixed cemetery. No Jewish tombstones could be found by the survey team, and it remains possible that the ground truth about this cemetery's Jewish origins cannot now be confirmed.
